geometry.note: The union of RESOLVE Ecoregions 2017's eight ecoregions named Sahara or Saharan and Tibesti–Jebel Uweinat, which Wikipedia (revision 1333931716) calls an ecoregion in the eastern Sahara. CC BY 4.0, credited on the map.

sahara.review: area: the Sahara is drawn as the union of RESOLVE Ecoregions 2017's Sahara ecoregions. Its southern edge runs at about 17–19°N (median 17.9°N; 14.8°N at 20–22°E; a small detached patch at 12.7°N in Darfur), north of the conventional 15–16°N boundary. Accepted by the user's decision (2026-09-26): the union claims no non-desert land, and a Sahara with no area was the larger gap on this map. Natural Earth's polygon, which runs to about 9°N, stays withheld.

geometry.note: The union of RESOLVE Ecoregions 2017's six ecoregions named Arabian … desert: Arabian desert, Arabian sand desert, Arabian-Persian Gulf coastal plain desert, North Arabian desert, East Arabian fog shrublands and sand desert, South Arabian plains and plateau desert. Left out: Red Sea-Arabian Desert shrublands (Egypt's Eastern Desert, a different feature) and the South and Southwest Arabian woodland, escarpment and montane ecoregions. CC BY 4.0, credited on the map.

arabian.review: area: the RESOLVE union covers 2,519,652 km², a little more than the 2,330,000 km² of List of deserts by area; it lies mostly in Saudi Arabia and reaches southern Iraq, southern Jordan, the Gulf states, western Oman and north-eastern Yemen, as the Arabian Desert article (Wikipedia revision 1373358142) describes, and takes in most of the Sinai and the Negev, which that article places in the Arabian Desert ecoregion. Accepted: it claims no land that is not desert.
